newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Zyuganov sees Russia as ship without captain.
newsitem.headline: Zyuganov sees Russia as ship without captain.

text.p: Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov, describing Russia as a ship without a captain, said on Monday that President Boris Yeltsin was incapacitated and no longer able to carry out his duties as head of state.
Zyuganov said the president, who is waiting for doctors to set a date for open heart surgery, had not worked since June 17, one day after the first round of the presidential poll.
"There should be a medical commission in the country and it should have the right to examine any official," Zyuganov told a meeting of Russian reporters.
"Russia is facing a crisis. Our ship is bumping in a stormy sea and there is no captain aboard, several people are trying to grab the wheel. This is not the way to navigate."
Zyuganov, 52, lost to Yeltsin in the second round of the presidential election in July before the president's state of health became public knowledge.
He has frequently demanded an independent commission to assess the president's health -- a proposal yet to be discussed by parliament.
On Monday he drew parallels between today's Russia and the situation before the 1917 revolution which brought the Bolsheviks to power.
"The tsar (the president) is incapacitated, he will no longer be able to work, and people know that," he said.
Yeltsin, 65, had two heart attacks last year and spent several months in hospital or recovering in a sanatorium.
He disappeared between the two rounds of the presidential election and admitted last month that he needed an operation to relieve congested arteries bringing blood to the heart.
Doctors say they will operate in the next two months and aides say he is working from hospital and from the sanatorium.

But Yeltsin has already delegated some powers to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who, together with chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais and security chief Alexander Lebed is managing many aspects of Russian policy during Yeltsin's absence.
Zyuganov's Communist Party is the largest single party in the State Duma lower house of parliament and Zyuganov heads a block of nationalist and left-wing parties.
He will be a key figure in a future election if Yeltsin hase to step down before his term in office expires in 2000.
Other challengers would probably be Chernomyrdin and Lebed, who on Sunday teamed up with the former head of Yeltsin's security service, Alexander Korzhakov.

NTV commercial television, commenting after Lebed asked voters to back Korzhakov's parliamentary bid in the arms manufacturing centre of Tula, said on Sunday the alliance could create a powerful "third force" in Russian politics.
Zyuganov said it was too early to say if his bloc would support Korzhakov.
The Tula seat fell vacant after Yeltsin appointed Lebed his security adviser and secretary of the powerful Security Council.
The communist leader said the three branches of power in Russia -- the government, the presidency and parliament -- should form a state council to work out how to resolve a crisis facing Russia.
"The situation...cannot be resolved using old traditional methods," he said. "I believe that nobody can cope with the situation single-handedly, the only way is to pool our efforts."
